chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Dharih who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'My night prayer was missed during travel; should I make it up during the day?' He said, 'Yes, if you are able to do so.'
ai.seo_question: How to make up missed night prayer during travel?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for missing *Salat al-Layl* (the night prayer) during travel, permitting its makeup (*qada*) during the day if the individual has the physical and mental capacity (*itaqa*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between obligatory prayers, which have fixed makeup times, and the highly recommended *Salat al-Layl*, which is flexible but contingent upon the believer's ability to perform it without undue hardship. The condition of *itaqa* underscores the principle that while the reward for night worship is immense, it is not an absolute burden that overrides the practical realities of travel or fatigue.
